chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Leaving Mutt's band as taxi dances declined
summary: Joe stayed six to eight months; pay dropped from forty-five dollars to percentage deals as taxi dances faded in 1928.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: How long did you stay with this Liberty Dance Orchestra?
No, no, it wasn't... Well, about six to eight months. Six to eight months. And things started getting real bad in '28, for the whole music business, for that matter. Taxi dances...
Nationwide or just here, you mean?

Well, particularly for taxi dances anyway. And yet the end, before I left... One reason why I really left was Papa Mutt, the guy couldn't pay the salaries, which was forty-five dollars a week, and we started working on a percentage deal, which some weeks you got thirty dollars, then it went down to like twenty... And I said to myself, "When I get a chance, I'm going on some place." I was ready to go back on a circus or something. In the meantime, this
